title: A chemically plausible route from simple feedstocks to evolving heredity

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a reproducible chemical system that starts with simple, geochemically defensible feedstocks and energy sources, produces information-bearing molecules, and carries them through repeated reproduction, heritable variation and selection. Its defining advance would be connecting these activities into a compatible experimental route, so that the products of chemical synthesis can become participants in an evolving molecular population. This is a proposed capability; the supplied evidence does not demonstrate the complete route.

RNA provides a concrete experimental approach because RNA molecules can carry sequence information and catalyze reactions. The reviewed 2024 work demonstrates an important part of this approach: an engineered RNA polymerase ribozyme enabled reproduction and evolution of a separate catalytic RNA. Connecting such molecular heredity to plausible nonliving starting materials would require substantially more than improving an isolated copying reaction.

Conceptual scope: the target is experimental feasibility under defensible chemical conditions. Establishing that a route actually operated on early Earth is a separate historical question requiring additional evidence. A successful experiment could reveal one possible origin of evolving heredity even if Earth's pathway used different molecules, environments or intermediate steps.

significance.text: Conditional significance: connecting plausible chemical production to sustained molecular heredity would demonstrate a route by which nonliving chemistry can acquire the capacity for cumulative evolution. The direct scientific consequence would be an experimentally tractable bridge between making molecules and maintaining functional information across generations. Describing that achievement as foundational is a scientific assessment of the proposed integration, rather than a ranking established by the supplied sources.

The 2024 RNA experiment illustrates why preserving information matters. Its higher-fidelity polymerase supported a succession of variants of the separate catalytic RNA with increasing fitness. An integrated feedstock-to-heredity system would extend this kind of result by connecting the supply and regeneration of molecular components to the evolutionary process itself.

Conditional downstream possibilities include testing how environmental cycles affect the emergence of heredity, comparing alternative chemical routes, and investigating which constraints permit molecular complexity to accumulate. The impact has important boundaries: evolving molecules would not by themselves establish cellular life, self-maintaining metabolism or unrestricted evolutionary complexity. Laboratory feasibility would also leave historical occurrence unresolved.

missing_breakthrough.text: Integration requirement: the missing capability is a compatible route linking feedstock chemistry, production of information-bearing polymers, copying, separation or release of copied strands, and repeated selection. Each stage must deliver usable material to the next under conditions the overall system can tolerate. The supplied evidence does not substantiate the full feedstock-formation chain or establish the present status of every approach to this integration; these remain requirements of the proposed innovation rather than a comprehensive finding about the field.

Replication fidelity is a documented barrier to a stronger form of autonomy. The 2024 study distinguishes evolution of a separate, smaller functional RNA from autonomous evolution of the polymerase that copies it. The authors identify further improvements in fidelity as necessary to maintain and evolve RNA enzymes as complex as the polymerase itself. Demonstrating evolution of a copied target therefore does not establish that the copying machinery can reproduce and evolve autonomously.

Replacing investigator-mediated regeneration is another concrete engineering challenge. The reviewed procedure used purification, reverse transcription, PCR and transcription to carry the evolving RNA through successive rounds. Those operations demonstrate how a laboratory can sustain the experiment, but they leave open how an integrated chemical system would recover usable products, regenerate its molecular population and continue selection without that biological machinery and repeated handling.

Engineering synthesis: a complete route would also need to reconcile component supply, energy input, molecular stability and copying conditions. It must distinguish productive reproduction from accumulation of unusable products, and heritable adaptation from enrichment caused solely by investigator choices. The supplied materials do not determine which chemical architecture could meet these requirements together.

current_state.text: In the study published on 4 March 2024, Papastavrou, Horning and Joyce demonstrated RNA-catalyzed evolution of a separate functional RNA, the hammerhead ribozyme. Eight rounds of evolution were conducted in parallel using two polymerases. The reviewed article reports maintenance of heritable information and progressively increasing fitness in the higher-fidelity lineage. This demonstrates reproduction and selection of a catalytic RNA with assistance from supplied copying machinery; it does not demonstrate autonomous evolution of the polymerase itself.

The scope of that demonstration includes substantial experimental intervention. Full-length products were purified by gel electrophoresis, and the procedure included reverse transcription, PCR and transcription to regenerate RNA. Consequently, the eight-round result does not establish continuous reproduction from simple geochemical feedstocks or independence from complex biological enzymes. The supplied review assessed the retained article text, but did not inspect linked supplementary materials or figure images.

The supplied research attributes a further result to Attwater and colleagues in a paper dated 28 May 2025: supplied trinucleotides and pH/freeze–thaw cycles reportedly enabled exponential RNA replication, including copying a fragment of an engineered polymerase ribozyme. It also states that the experiment did not generate that ribozyme and its substrates from simple geochemical feedstocks. These details remain unverified within the supplied evidence package: the retained PubMed artifact contains only a cookie-access message, which cannot establish the article's identity, experimental results or limits. The research's earlier statement that an abstract and figure descriptions were inspected is not substantiated by that retained artifact. This access limitation does not show that the reported result is false.

Evidence boundary: these materials establish a dated, partial demonstration of RNA heredity and evolution, while leaving the complete proposed route unestablished. The supplied search record is empty, so the package cannot determine the latest state of the field as of 1 November 2026. It also cannot establish that no other integrated approach has succeeded.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: begin with explicitly specified, geochemically defensible feedstocks and energy inputs, generate information-bearing polymers, and sustain repeated sequence-dependent reproduction and selection. The operational specification should identify all supplied components, environmental cycles and permitted interventions, including any initial catalyst or seed. It should show how continued reproduction proceeds without repeated investigator-supplied purification or complex biological enzymes. These are proposed criteria for this innovation, not established community standards.
completion_criteria.label: Geochemical feedstocks yield polymers with sequence-dependent reproduction and selection

completion_criteria.text: Proposed evidence for heredity and evolution should connect sequence changes to inherited functional differences across successive generations. Controls should distinguish reproduction from persistence of the starting material and distinguish selection from transient enrichment or investigator-driven replacement. The experiment should document whether the copying machinery is merely supplied, replenished externally, reproduced by the system, or itself capable of evolution; these represent materially different levels of autonomy.
completion_criteria.label: Sequence changes confer inherited functional differences across successive generations

completion_criteria.text: The reviewed RNA study provides a concrete benchmark for interpreting such evidence: propagation and evolution of a functional target can be demonstrated while regeneration still depends on purification and enzyme-mediated laboratory steps. A convincing integrated demonstration would need to account explicitly for how the functions performed by those steps are supplied within the proposed chemical route.
completion_criteria.label: Chemical route accounts for purification and enzyme-mediated regeneration functions

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and practical boundaries should include independent replication, disclosed concentrations and yields, documented material and energy inputs, and testing across a defined range of sequences and environmental conditions. The number of generations needed to support sustained selection should be justified against carryover, depletion and transient enrichment; the supplied materials provide no established numerical threshold. Finite experiments would establish demonstrated breadth under specified conditions, not literal universality or unlimited evolutionary potential.
completion_criteria.label: Independent replication with disclosed inputs, yields and tested boundaries

completion_criteria.text: Proposed historical boundary: a reproducible laboratory route would satisfy a feasibility claim only within its demonstrated conditions. Claims that the route occurred on early Earth would require additional evidence connecting those conditions, feedstocks and processes to relevant environments and times.
completion_criteria.label: Historical claims connect demonstrated chemistry to early Earth environments

related_concepts.text: Roster-based comparison: BCH-03, “A self-maintaining, evolvable cell assembled from defined components,” shares the goal of sustained evolution but centers on cellular organization and self-maintenance. BCH-04 centers on the chemical emergence of heredity from plausible feedstocks and need not initially produce a cell. Neither achievement would automatically establish the other.

Roster-based comparison: BCH-07, “Autonomous heredity in a chemically distinct genetic polymer,” overlaps directly in copying, fidelity and inherited variation. Its defining distinction is the genetic polymer's chemical identity and autonomous heredity. BCH-04 instead requires a plausible chemical route from feedstocks into evolution; that route could involve RNA or another polymer, but a distinct polymer alone would not satisfy it.

Roster-based comparison: BCH-01, “General design of enzymes for new chemical reactions,” and BCH-02, “Predict biochemical function from molecular sequence and environment,” could contribute catalysts or predictive understanding useful for investigating a route to heredity. Their targets are design and prediction. Successful designed catalysts or accurate predictions would not by themselves demonstrate spontaneous chemical production, reproduction and selection under BCH-04's proposed constraints.

Roster-based comparison: BCH-09, “Predict and control the biochemical organization of condensates,” could intersect with questions of concentration and molecular organization in a proposed route. BCH-10, “Predict modification-dependent biochemical networks,” could intersect with understanding how chemical changes alter interacting molecular processes. Both concern distinct organizational or predictive capabilities; neither requires demonstrating an origin of evolving heredity.

Roster-based comparison: BCH-05, “Routine, comprehensive single-cell proteoform reading,” BCH-06, “A multiplexed biochemical flight recorder for living cells,” and BCH-11, “Routine structural reading of complex glycans,” are measurement capabilities that might inform particular experimental systems. Their subjects and completion targets remain distinct from producing an evolving molecular population from simple feedstocks. BCH-08, “Resolve the nitrogenase reaction cycle during nitrogen fixation,” concerns the mechanism of a specific enzyme system; any connection to feedstock chemistry would depend on a particular proposed route and is not established by the supplied evidence.

change_log.change: Preserved BCH-04's identity and framed the innovation as an integrated, proposed route from plausible feedstocks to evolving molecular heredity.
change_log.reason: The central concept remains coherent even though the supplied evidence demonstrates only parts of the route.

change_log.change: Expanded the 2024 result to identify the hammerhead target, eight rounds, parallel polymerase comparison and higher-fidelity lineage's increasing fitness.
change_log.reason: The validated review supplies substantive experimental detail that clarifies the demonstrated scope.

change_log.change: Added purification, reverse transcription, PCR and transcription to the description of the 2024 procedure.
change_log.reason: These interventions explain why the demonstration does not establish an integrated prebiotic system or autonomous polymerase evolution.

change_log.change: Retained the reported 2025 Attwater result as explicitly unverified supplied-research content, including its reported fragment-copying scope and feedstock limitation.
change_log.reason: The retained artifact contains no scientific content. Preserving the reported detail with qualification avoids treating missing evidence as either verification or disproof.

change_log.change: Replaced the earlier claim of substantiated Attwater abstract and figure inspection with the documented access limitation.
change_log.reason: The supplied review found only a cookie-access message in the retained artifact.

change_log.change: Separated experimental feasibility, autonomous evolution, cellular life and historical occurrence.
change_log.reason: These are different achievements; none follows automatically from evolution of a separate functional RNA.

change_log.change: Made completion criteria explicitly proposed and added intervention accounting, controls, reproducibility and bounded interpretation of finite tests.
change_log.reason: The supplied materials establish neither consensus thresholds nor a numerical definition of sustained selection.

change_log.change: Qualified field-wide and freshness claims, and added roster-based comparisons without merging entries.
change_log.reason: The empty search record cannot establish the latest field status, and the roster supplies distinct innovation identities rather than evidence of demonstrated relationships.

unresolved_issues: Substantive Attwater source text remains unavailable in the supplied package. The reported 2025 replication, fragment-copying result and experimental limitations require verification.

The review recommended restoring Attwater details after inspecting substantive text. No inspection was authorized here; the details are therefore retained only as attributed, unverified research reports.
The package does not substantiate feedstock formation or compatibility of the entire proposed chemical chain, and does not determine whether another approach has achieved the integration.
The latest field status as of 1 November 2026 remains unassessed because the supplied search record is empty.
Geochemical defensibility, permitted initial seeds and interventions, sufficient generations, and acceptable dependence on externally supplied catalysts need operational definitions.
The reviewed 2024 article's linked supplementary materials and figure images were not inspected.
No supplied evidence establishes that a laboratory route to evolving heredity occurred historically on early Earth.

brief.title: A route from simple chemicals to evolving molecules
possible: Scientists could start with simple chemicals and build a system whose molecules reproduce, pass on changes and evolve across generations. This would let them test a possible route from nonliving chemistry to heredity—the passing of information from one generation to the next.
why: Connecting chemical production to heredity would help explain how useful molecular information can survive and accumulate. Researchers could compare chemical routes and test how environmental cycles help evolving populations gain complexity.

sources.showed: RNA is a molecule that can carry information and speed chemical reactions. Using supplied short RNA building blocks, an engineered RNA copying molecule and cycles of acidity, freezing and thawing, the team sustained repeated copying, including a fragment of the copying molecule itself.
sources.quote: When combined with coupled pH and freeze–thaw cycles, this enabled exponential replication of both (+) and (−) strands of double-stranded RNAs, including a fragment of the ribozyme itself.
sources.cited_for: Chemical cycles and short building blocks can keep copied RNA strands available for further copying.
sources.not_established: The experiment did not produce its copying molecule and building blocks from simple starting chemicals.

sources.who: Nikolaos Papastavrou, David P. Horning and Gerald F. Joyce
sources.showed: An engineered RNA copying molecule supported reproduction and evolution of a separate RNA that cuts RNA. Variants became better at reproducing while retaining cutting activity.
sources.quote: The increase in fitness was attributable to specific mutations that improved the replicability of the hammerhead, counterbalanced by a small decrease in hammerhead activity.
sources.cited_for: Accurate RNA copying can preserve inherited function while beneficial changes accumulate.
sources.not_established: The copying machinery did not reproduce and evolve independently, and propagation relied on purification and biological enzymes.

shown: Researchers have demonstrated separate pieces of the route: Attwater and colleagues sustained RNA copying through environmental cycles, while Papastavrou and colleagues maintained an evolving functional RNA population. Neither demonstration connected simple starting chemicals to sustained heredity.
missing: A connected chemical route must make information-bearing molecules from plausible starting materials and keep them reproducing under compatible conditions.
The system must supply the functions now performed by repeated laboratory purification and enzyme-assisted regeneration.
Copying must remain accurate enough to preserve useful information as evolving molecules become more complex.

milestones.label: Simple starting chemicals yield molecules that reproduce and undergo selection
milestones.explanation: A system would have to turn geologically plausible starting chemicals into molecules that repeatedly reproduce and undergo selection. This would connect chemical production to evolution.

milestones.label: Sequence changes produce inherited differences in function
milestones.explanation: Changes in the order of molecular building blocks would have to cause functional differences inherited across generations. This would distinguish evolution from persistence or temporary enrichment.

milestones.label: The chemical route sustains regeneration
milestones.explanation: The route would have to provide the functions performed by laboratory purification and enzyme-assisted regeneration. This would explain how usable molecules remain available for continued reproduction.

milestones.label: Independent teams reproduce the result within tested limits
milestones.explanation: Independent teams would have to reproduce the system with disclosed inputs and yields across defined sequences and conditions. This would establish its reliability and the breadth of sustained selection.

milestones.label: Historical claims connect the chemistry to early Earth
milestones.explanation: A claim that the route occurred on early Earth would need evidence linking its chemicals and conditions to relevant environments and times. This would connect laboratory feasibility to planetary history.

uncertain: Which starting chemicals, initial catalysts and environmental cycles can work together remains open.
How many generations establish sustained selection, rather than temporary enrichment or carryover, needs a justified criterion.
How much external support is acceptable must be defined, including whether the copying machinery must itself reproduce and evolve.

page.title: Prebiotic emergence of Darwinian evolution
page.definition: A laboratory chemical route converts small molecules available before life into a reproducing population. Changes in molecular sequence pass to descendants, and variants with some inherited changes leave more descendants than others. Pairs of RNA enzymes can already assemble each other from supplied RNA fragments. In the prebiotic route, the genetic polymers and the machinery that copies them must themselves arise under conditions compatible with the proposed planetary environment.

goal.need: Earth is the only world known to host life, and little geological evidence survives from the time when prebiotic chemistry began. Reactions that work separately can interfere with one another when joined. A connected route would show how heredity and selection could arise in a particular planetary setting and give the search for life elsewhere a set of conditions to look for. Identifying the route life actually took on Earth would still require geological evidence.

figures.note: These are components of one engineered system, not minimum lengths required for heredity.

statements.quote: Establish replicating, catalytic systems capable of evolution and construct laboratory models of metabolism in primitive living systems.

statements.quote: Connect Abiotic Formation of Organic Molecules to Emergence of Life
statements.context: The objective connects open-ended Darwinian evolution with the joint evolution of small-molecule reaction networks, polymers that perform functions or carry information, and selectively permeable compartments.

completion.title: A connected prebiotic chemical route produces a self-sustaining population undergoing Darwinian evolution.
completion.criterion: Demonstrate one connected laboratory route from specified small-molecule feedstocks and energy sources to a self-sustaining chemical population exhibiting reproduction, heritable variation and differential reproductive success. Feedstocks, catalysts and environmental transitions must be supported by a specified prebiotic setting. Genetic polymers and their copying machinery must originate through the route, rather than enter as engineered seeds or be regenerated by external biological enzymes. Continued supply of feedstocks and energy is permitted. No fixed yield, fidelity or generation count is imposed.
completion.set_by: Atlas synthesis of NASA's prebiotic-chemistry objectives and the origins-of-life working definition; no external operational test for their integration was found.
completion.basis: Searches of NASA's 1998 and 2003 roadmaps, Ames Objective 7.1, the National Academies' decadal strategy, and origins-of-life challenge and prize documents found no integrated test specifying allowed seeds, interventions and duration. This criterion joins the published goals of chemistry constrained by prebiotic environments and self-sustaining Darwinian evolution.

milestones.title: Laboratory chemistry produces organic compounds under simulated primordial planetary conditions.
milestones.criterion: Produce and identify organic compounds in a laboratory simulation of specified primordial planetary conditions.
milestones.set_by: NASA, 2003 Astrobiology Roadmap, Objective 3.1, example investigations.
milestones.threshold_quote: Identify the organic compounds and complexes produced under primordial planetary conditions through laboratory simulation experiments.

milestones.title: Chemical pathways produce genetic polymers under early-Earth environmental constraints.
milestones.criterion: Demonstrate a chemical pathway that forms a genetic polymer under thermodynamic and environmental conditions consistent with a specified early-Earth setting.
milestones.set_by: NASA, 1998 Astrobiology Roadmap, Objective 2, implementation; genetic polymers are the nucleic-acid component of this broader objective.
milestones.threshold_quote: Conduct ground-based laboratory research on chemical pathways leading to the emergence of the macromolecules of life. These pathways should be consistent with the thermodynamic and environmental constraints on the early earth.

milestones.title: A molecular chemical system sustains repeated replication.
milestones.criterion: Demonstrate repeated molecular replication in a laboratory chemical system by showing that products of replication participate in producing further copies.
milestones.threshold_quote: Through laboratory experiments, develop and characterize self-replicating systems based on diverse molecules and recognition mechanisms.

milestones.title: Artificial chemical populations undergo mutation and natural selection.
milestones.criterion: Demonstrate mutation in a reproducing chemical population and show that a heritable difference affects the relative reproductive success of the variants under the test conditions.
milestones.threshold_quote: Without regard to how life actually emerged on Earth, create and study artificial chemical systems that undergo mutation and natural selection in the laboratory.

milestones.title: A chemical population sustains Darwinian evolution while maintaining its own copying machinery.
milestones.criterion: Show that a chemical population reproduces with heritable variation and differential reproductive success, and that it makes the functional copying machinery used in subsequent rounds. The experiment may start with preassembled genetic polymers and receive substrates and energy throughout.
milestones.set_by: Origins-of-life working convention described by Gerald Joyce in the Institute of Medicine's 2011 workshop summary, pages 24–26; autonomous RNA evolution is also an explicit criterion in Papastavrou and colleagues' 2024 paper.
milestones.threshold_quote: a self-sustained chemical system capable of undergoing Darwinian evolution.

milestones.title: A molecular copying error passes to descendants in a later round of replication.
milestones.criterion: Show that molecular replication produces an altered sequence and that replication of the variant transmits the change to its descendants.
milestones.set_by: NASA Astrobiology Strategy 2015, chapter 2, question on information transmission and chemical evolution.
milestones.threshold_quote: What kinds of molecules can be replicated with errors, where the errors themselves are replicable?

not_found: No external operational protocol for the complete feedstock-to-evolution route was found.
No universal minimum yield, copying fidelity or generation count for evolving prebiotic heredity was found.
No report demonstrating the complete connected route was found.
No statement in the NASA strategies or National Academies reports examined judged a laboratory route to evolving prebiotic chemistry infeasible or unworthy of pursuit.

results.finding: Two RNA lineages underwent eight rounds of replication and selection.
results.detail: Each round included RNA-catalyzed synthesis of both strands. Reverse transcription, PCR and transcription regenerated the population between rounds.
results.quote: This process was continued for eight rounds for each lineage, after which materials from each round were analyzed by deep sequencing to determine the course of hammerhead evolution.

results.finding: Five evolved hammerhead variants had three- to eightfold higher calculated fitness than the starting RNA.
results.detail: Two lineages were evolved; biochemical fitness measurements used three replicates. The population was regenerated between rounds using reverse transcription, PCR and transcription.
results.quote: The net effect, multiplying the yields from plus- and minus-strand synthesis and the requisite RNA-cleavage activity of the plus strand, is that the evolved variants have an overall three- to eightfold improvement in fitness compared to Seq0 ( Fig. 4 B ).

results.finding: Prebiotic laboratory chemistry produced precursors of 3 classes of biomolecules; sample size not reported.
results.detail: Experiments used prebiotically plausible intermediates, UV light and hydrogen sulfide. The proposed Hadean Earth setting is a geochemical scenario; the complete reaction network was not demonstrated in one pot.
results.quote: We show that precursors of ribonucleotides, amino acids and lipids can all be derived by reductive homologation of hydrogen cyanide and some of its derivatives and thus that all the cellular subsystems could have arisen simultaneously through common chemistry.

results.finding: Prebiotic one-pot synthesis produced phosphorylated nucleosides at 19% yield relative to cytidine; sample size not reported.
results.detail: The experiment used a phosphate-containing mineral and evaporation at 85°C, simulating wet-dry conditions proposed for early Earth. It produced RNA building blocks, not a reproducing system.
results.quote:
LC-MS analysis of the reaction now showed formation of phosphorylated 
nucleosides (Fig. 3A) in remarkable 19% yield relative to cytidine (Fig. 3B and Fig. S7).

results.finding: Primer-free RNA synthesis in two conditions, with and without an added template pool, produced RNAs up to 60 nucleotides long.
results.detail: Both conditions received activated RNA triplets and an engineered polymerase ribozyme.
results.quote: We observed products ranging from 6 to 60 nt in length, with many (25–75%) in both seeded and unseeded reactions showing some complementarity to the TPR ribozyme sequence

results.finding: Across two starting-strand conditions, second-round products showed that first-round RNA products served as templates in cycle 2.
results.quote: This indicates that in cycle 2, the product strands of cycle 1 are used as templates, providing a foundation for exponential RNA amplification.

results.finding: Sequencing of 10,880 reads from γ-fragment replication detected altered RNA products alongside accurate copies.
results.quote:
Sequencing the products of γ
D
-seeded reactions confirmed the replication of accurate γ
+
sequences alongside a number of partially homologous sequences probably derived from incomplete extension products undergoing recombination, and even some unanticipated products complementary to the TPR t1 subunit

results.finding: Three emergent RNA length classes amplified at different rates, with the fastest estimated at 1.37-fold per cycle.
results.detail: The authors inferred that early incorporation of a supplied pentanucleotide generated shorter products with a reciprocal primer-binding site.

results.finding: One polymerase ribozyme fragment amplified by up to 1.26-fold per cycle.
results.detail: The active polymerase was supplied in the reaction mix and replenished during serial dilution.
results.quote: These results show that (1) a ribozyme can exponentially replicate part of itself from short building blocks, (2) this ‘fragmentary’ self-replication can occur in a ‘one-pot’ cycled reaction and (3) ribozymes can initiate replication on themselves, even in the absence of a seed template.

results.finding: Hammerhead RNA was reciprocally copied over eight rounds in two lineages.
results.detail: The protocol used reverse transcription, PCR and forward transcription to regenerate the selected population between rounds.
results.quote: During each round, the hammerhead RNA was copied by the polymerase to yield its complement, which in turn was copied by the polymerase to generate new hammerhead ribozymes, which were required to catalyze an RNA-cleavage reaction.

results.finding: In one 71-89 hammerhead lineage, the Seq2 cluster carried forward a peak sequence with two mutations.
results.detail: The authors inferred descent from sequence data and separately copied variants because the mixed-population protocol could not track individual molecules directly.
results.quote: The Seq0 cluster declined from the outset, initially replaced by a group of very closely related sequences that subsequently coalesced to form the Seq2 cluster, with a peak sequence containing two mutations relative to Seq0.

results.finding: In a six-sequence hammerhead competition, Seq15 and Seq3 each accounted for about 30% of progeny.
results.detail: The evolved variants copied more efficiently despite reduced cleavage activity. A control found no significant enrichment from reverse transcription and PCR alone.
results.quote: As a consequence, the progeny of Seq15 and Seq3 each comprise ~30% of the population following a single round of evolution, compared to only 4% for Seq0.

results.finding: One hammerhead lineage maintained catalytic activity through eight rounds of evolution with a supplied polymerase.
results.detail: Reverse transcription, PCR and forward transcription regenerated selected hammerheads between rounds. A separate directed-evolution experiment improved the polymerase using external enzymes.
results.quote: In contrast, for the population replicated by the 71-89 polymerase, catalytic activity was maintained throughout the eight rounds.

results.finding: Activated uridine cyclic phosphate was obtained at 42% after UV irradiation of activated cytidine cyclic phosphate. Replicate count unspecified.
results.detail: The authors relate heating, dehydration, cooling, rehydration and UV exposure to possible early-Earth environments. The timing of separate glycolaldehyde and glyceraldehyde supplies remains unresolved.

results.finding: Phosphorylation of arabinose anhydronucleoside in formamide gave 46% activated cytidine cyclic phosphate. Replicate count unspecified.
results.detail: The route ends with activated monomers. RNA polymerization appears as a result from cited work.

results.finding: Wet–dry cycling of the A/U/G/C cyclic nucleotide mixture (n = 2 independent replicates) produced RNA oligomers up to 10 nucleotides long.
results.quote:
revealing the emergence of
distinct peaks at longer retention times corresponding to high-yield
production of RNA oligomers up to at least 10 nucleotides in length.

results.finding: The A/U/G/C cyclic nucleotide mixture (n = 2 independent replicates) reached 36% RNA oligomerization yield under alkaline wet–dry cycling.
results.detail: The study supplied cyclic nucleotide monomers. Mass spectrometry resolved base composition but could not distinguish base order or the two phosphodiester linkage types.

of 30 μM

results.finding: Triplicate ribose phosphorylation runs with borate yielded 47.90 mM ribose 1,2-cyclic phosphate.
results.detail: Table 1 reports the 24-hour concentrations. The study also detected ribose 1,2-cyclic phosphate when the activating reagent formed in situ from cyclic trimetaphosphate and ammonia.
results.quote: This shows that ribose-1,2-cyclic phosphate can be formed from inorganic cyclic triphosphate, ribose, and ammonia, continuously in the presence of borate.

results.finding: Basalt glass and borate produced RNA oligomers from uridine triphosphate, with the longest estimated at >100 nucleotides. Replicate count unreported.
results.detail: The length estimate comes from gel migration. Polymerization used supplied uridine triphosphate in a separate experiment from the upstream precursor synthesis.
results.quote: The longest are interpreted as being >100 nts.

results.finding: One cross-replicating RNA enzyme pair formed full-length RNA from four supplied oligonucleotide substrates.
results.detail: The ligation assays used prepared oligonucleotides and engineered ribozymes.
results.quote: The F1 enzyme was converted to a pair of cross-replicating enzymes (F1 and F1′), which were supplied with 5 μM each of the four substrates needed to support exponential growth.

results.finding: One F1/F1′ RNA enzyme pair sustained cross-replication over 50 serial-transfer rounds.
results.detail: Each round ran for 45 minutes at 47 °C. The reported overall dilution was 10¹⁰⁰-fold.
results.quote: Fifty successive rounds of cross- replication, with transfer of 1% of reacted materials (100-fold dilution) after each round.

results.finding: Sequencing 31 round-10 RNA ligase clones revealed sporadic changes outside the initially mutagenized region.
results.detail: The study did not quantify these sporadic changes in the prose or track them across rounds.
results.quote: Mutations can arise outside the region that was originally mutagenized due to polymerase errors during amplification. These mutations occurred sporadically and appear to have little functional consequence.

results.finding: In separate assays of two RNA ligase genotypes, F1 self-replicated 23-fold faster than E1.
results.detail: The directed-evolution protocol selected ligation products by capture and regenerated the population by RT-PCR and transcription.

results.finding: One F1/F1′ ribozyme pair regenerated its copying machinery across 50 serial-transfer rounds.
results.detail: The serial-transfer experiment used a fixed set of substrates for the two engineered partners.
results.quote: No enzymes are added to the new reaction other than those that are carried over in the transfer.

results.finding: In a five-clone RNA mixture, four clones co-replicated for at least 22 serial transfers.
Across 18 late-stage sampling points, sequencing traced an HL3 descendant genotype with at least 10 distinct mutations.
results.detail: Inheritance was inferred from successive genotypes in the sequence phylogeny.
results.quote: Other RNAs in HL2 accumulated independent mutations around round 129 and formed another set of branches, named HL3, which contains a genotype (HL3–228) that remained in the final round with at least 10 distinct mutations and also exhibited markedly different characteristics from those in HL2 as shown later.

results.finding: In a five-clone RNA mixture, four evolved variants sustained replication while HL3 washed out.
results.detail: The clone assays link differential replication to heritable differences in which RNA templates the evolved replicases can copy.

results.finding: Among five evolved RNA clones, the replicase produced from HL2 copied all five.
results.detail: Fresh reconstituted E. coli translation system supplied EF-Tu and EF-Ts, which associate with the RNA-encoded subunit to form active replicase.
results.quote: HL2–228 replicase replicated all five RNA clones.

results.finding: Synthetic molecular replicators self-replicated in 2 laboratory systems.
results.detail: The supplied preview gives the number of systems and omits the number of replication rounds.
results.quote: Here we show the emergence of Darwinian evolution in two systems of self-replicating molecules in which natural selection favours replicator mutants best capable of catalysing the production of the precursors required for their own replication.

results.finding: Replicator mutants were observed in 2 self-replicating chemical systems.
results.detail: The preview reports variant classes and selection at the population level. It gives no sequence-resolved parent–descendant result.
results.quote: Here we show the emergence of Darwinian evolution in two systems of self-replicating molecules in which natural selection favours replicator mutants best capable of catalysing the production of the precursors required for their own replication.

results.finding: In 2 synthetic replicator systems, selection favoured mutants better able to catalyse production of their own replication precursors.
results.detail: Mutants activated a photocatalytic cofactor that generated singlet oxygen and accelerated conversion of peptide-based dithiols into disulfide precursors.
results.quote: Here we show the emergence of Darwinian evolution in two systems of self-replicating molecules in which natural selection favours replicator mutants best capable of catalysing the production of the precursors required for their own replication.

results.finding: In 2 evolving synthetic replicator systems, selected mutants catalysed production of their own replication precursors.
results.detail: The photocatalytic cofactor assists precursor production. The supplied text leaves the production and later use of new copying machinery unverified.
results.quote: Here we show the emergence of Darwinian evolution in two systems of self-replicating molecules in which natural selection favours replicator mutants best capable of catalysing the production of the precursors required for their own replication.

results.finding: One pair of cross-replicating RNA ligases amplified more than 10⁸-fold per enzyme during serial transfer.
results.detail: The optimized ligases amplified at 42°C. Fresh oligonucleotide substrates replenished the reaction at each transfer.
results.quote:
Exponential growth was
maintained throughout 30 hours total of incubation,
with an overall amplification of greater than 108-
fold for each of the two enzymes (Fig. 2B).

results.finding: Cross-replicating RNA ligases yielded 93 recombinant clones among 100 sequenced.
results.detail: Endpoint sequencing established the presence of newly formed variants. The growth assay for A5B3 and B5′A3′ showed that a recombinant pair could propagate its altered sequence.
results.quote:
but once a mismatched substrate is bound and
ligated, it forms a recombinant enzyme that also can
cross-replicate.

results.finding: RNA ligases seeded as 12 parental pairs produced recombinant descendants that made up 93% of 100 sequenced clones.
results.detail: E1 grew fastest with its own substrates. A5B3 grew fastest in the full substrate pool used for competition.
results.quote:
In the presence of their cognate substrates alone,
E1 remained the most efficient replicator, but in the
presence of all 48 substrates, the most efficient
replicator was A5B3 (Fig. 3C).

results.finding: A population seeded with 12 RNA ligase pairs sustained amplification for 20 rounds while producing its own copying catalysts.
results.detail: Each transfer carried over 5% of the reaction mixture into fresh RNA substrates. The replicated ligases provided the catalytic machinery for the next round.
results.quote:
Beginning with 12 pairs of cross-replicating RNA enzymes (Fig. 1C),
amplification was sustained for 20 successive rounds of ~20-fold amplification and 20-fold dilution.

results.finding: Across five Hadean rock-glass analogues tested, three produced prominent polymer bands. Chemical analysis identified the diabase product as polyribonucleic acid.
results.detail: Quartz and water-only controls yielded no detectable polyribonucleic acid.
results.quote: This study shows that various mafic rock glasses almost certainly present on the surface of the Hadean Earth catalyze the formation of polyribonucleic acid in water starting from nucleoside triphosphates.

results.finding: In a comparison of five rock-glass types, the authors reported glass-made polyribonucleic acid averaging 90–150 nucleotides in the discussion.
results.detail: The abstract gives a different average-length range of 100–300 nucleotides. The analyses leave open the presence of 2′,5′ linkages and branching.
results.quote: Both gel electrophoresis and ultrafiltration show that this polyribonucleic acid is, on average, 90–150 nucleotides in length.

results.finding: Wet–dry cycling produced uridine chains up to 53 nucleotides long by mass spectrometry. The number of independent samples was unreported.
results.detail: Polymer abundance rose during the first two cycles, then declined for medium and long chains in the third cycle as hydrolysis and possible degradation became more prominent.
results.quote: Mass spectrometric analysis reveals uridine monophosphate oligomers up to 53 nucleotides, with an abundance of 35 and 43 nt in length.

results.finding: Valine-catalysed reactions with all four cyclic ribonucleotides formed RNA oligomers up to 5 nucleotides long across three independent experiments.
results.detail: The experiments started with supplied cyclic ribonucleotides and produced short RNA strands. The criterion specifies polymer formation and sets no minimum length or requirement to demonstrate copying.
results.quote:
The copolymerisation from the full base set G/C/A/U (with Val, Gly
or Lys) conﬁrmed this trend. Here, we even found that for 2 −5-mers,
the fraction of G was reduced (Fig.4b).

results.finding: P1-lig Flexizyme sustained self-assembly for 648 hours across seeded and unseeded serial-dilution time courses.
results.detail: Each transfer supplied fresh RNA fragments and glycine donor. The paper reports one time course per seeding condition in Fig. 5 without specifying a replicate count for the serial-dilution experiment.
results.quote: With each subsequent dilution, the concentration of the newly synthesized P1-lig Flexizyme increased until it matched the concentration present before dilution.

results.finding: Synthetic hexamer replicators produced a mutant that accounted for 36% of new hexamers, and different variants dominated under different selection regimes. Seeding replicate count unstated.
results.detail: The outflow experiment was repeated. Equal removal rates favored faster replication, while chemical reduction favored a variant that combined replication with resistance to destruction.
results.quote: Seeding experiments confirmed that the building-block sequence was moderately heritable and that sequence replication is error prone, whereas the fidelity for copying ring size is high.

results.finding: Cooperative Rep- and NDK-RNAs reproduced for up to 79 rounds across two successive serial-transfer experiments.
results.detail: The researchers replenished the cell-free translation system at every transfer. It supplied EF-Tu and EF-Ts, which are required for the RNA-encoded catalytic subunit to form an active replicase.
results.quote: In the second long-term replication experiment with the e2R0 pair, we changed the dilution rate from 5- to 100-fold when the RNA concentration reached around 100 nM and successfully continued the replication of both Rep- and NDK-RNAs for 79 rounds

results.finding: Six clonal N96 RNA populations accumulated and inherited replication-generated substitutions over 200 serial transfers.
results.detail: The authors inferred inheritance from consensus haplotypes and mutation-frequency trajectories across transfers. The system used a protein replicase and supplied cell-free translation machinery.
results.quote: Overall, antagonistic host–parasite interactions helped maintain replication capacity and accelerated mutation fixation, promoting divergence between populations but not diversification within populations

definition = "A laboratory chemical route converts small molecules available before life into a reproducing population. Changes in molecular sequence pass to descendants, and variants with some inherited changes leave more descendants than others. Pairs of RNA enzymes can already assemble each other from supplied RNA fragments. In the prebiotic route, the genetic polymers and the machinery that copies them must themselves arise under conditions compatible with the proposed planetary environment.". Reason: The definition leaves natural selection unexplained and does not say how close existing RNA systems come.

goal.need = "Earth is the only world known to host life, and little geological evidence survives from the time when prebiotic chemistry began. Reactions that work separately can interfere with one another when joined. A connected route would show how heredity and selection could arise in a particular planetary setting and give the search for life elsewhere a set of conditions to look for. Identifying the route life actually took on Earth would still require geological evidence.". Reason: The current rationale reports the copying fidelity of one experiment but omits the geological evidence gap and the scientific value of connecting the reactions.

add statement by NASA Ames Research Center, Space Science and Astrobiology Strategic Plan, Objective 7.1, 2019: "Connect Abiotic Formation of Organic Molecules to Emergence of Life". Reason: The 2019 objective names the connection directly and identifies the components behind the earlier quotation’s phrase “all of these components.”

edit m1: criterion = "Produce and identify organic compounds in a laboratory simulation of specified primordial planetary conditions."; threshold_quote = "Identify the organic compounds and complexes produced under primordial planetary conditions through laboratory simulation experiments."; threshold_ref = 6; refs = [6, 23, 8]. Reason: The criterion includes one nucleotide-synthesis result and omits the simpler amino-acid demonstration that also meets NASA’s objective.

edit m2: criterion = "Demonstrate a chemical pathway that forms a genetic polymer under thermodynamic and environmental conditions consistent with a specified early-Earth setting."; threshold_quote = "Conduct ground-based laboratory research on chemical pathways leading to the emergence of the macromolecules of life. These pathways should be consistent with the thermodynamic and environmental constraints on the early earth."; threshold_ref = 5. Reason: The chain length, supplied primer and replication details belong to the Ferris result and are not conditions imposed by the roadmap.

edit m3: criterion = "Demonstrate repeated molecular replication in a laboratory chemical system by showing that products of replication participate in producing further copies."; threshold_quote = "Through laboratory experiments, develop and characterize self-replicating systems based on diverse molecules and recognition mechanisms."; threshold_ref = 2. Reason: The existing criterion gives the cycle counts of two experiments without stating what distinguishes repeated replication from a single copying reaction.

add milestone after m3: "A molecular copying error passes to descendants in a later round of replication.". Reason: Repeated replication can preserve a starting sequence without showing that a newly introduced change passes to descendants.

edit m4: criterion = "Demonstrate mutation in a reproducing chemical population and show that a heritable difference affects the relative reproductive success of the variants under the test conditions."; threshold_quote = "Without regard to how life actually emerged on Earth, create and study artificial chemical systems that undergo mutation and natural selection in the laboratory."; threshold_ref = 6; refs = [6, 7, 1]. Reason: The existing criterion mixes the test for selection with the round count, assays and regeneration procedure of one RNA experiment.

edit m5: criterion = "Show that a chemical population reproduces with heritable variation and differential reproductive success, and that it makes the functional copying machinery used in subsequent rounds. The experiment may start with preassembled genetic polymers and receive substrates and energy throughout."; threshold_quote = "a self-sustained chemical system capable of undergoing Darwinian evolution."; threshold_ref = 7; refs = [7, 19, 1, 11]. Reason: The existing criterion describes separate strand-synthesis reactions without specifying how to tell whether an evolving population regenerates its copying machinery.
